correctness.rationale: For all integers \(n\ge3\), local descending-domination conditions and acyclic orientations yield a bijection with compatible three-color cyclic words excluding monochromatic vertex covers. Cyclic transfer traces count these words with their exact face cardinalities. Eigenvalues at \(t=-1\) prove the 12-periodic Euler law. Direct enumeration of all filtration permutations for \(3\le n\le8\) and integer polynomial checks through \(n=100\) agree; the all-parameter proof is symbolic.

originality.rationale: Relevant full primary texts were compared by logical implication: Knudson–Owens–White supply only top-face counts and finite homology computations of the full cycle complex; Chari–Joswig count the different ordinary Morse complex; Fernández supplies the underlying filtration theory but not the strong-complex enumeration. No indexed or published equivalent to the complete all-n strong face polynomial emerged; potential unindexed coverage remains a risk.
residual_risks: An older equivalently reparameterized enumeration of colored cyclic incidences may exist outside available indexes.
A general counting statement from the ordinary-Morse literature might be adaptable, but the checked statements do not imply strong face counts without an additional filtration restriction analysis.

value.rationale: A natural all-n invariant—the entire face vector of the complete, generally nonpure cycle strong Morse matching complex—is determined by fixed-size transfer matrices, including lengths beyond the published \(n\le21\) homology computations. A nontrivial exact 12-periodic reduced Euler characteristic constrains future homology calculations. This is not an arbitrary selected numerical example; \(n=22\) illustrates the general result and does not purport to classify homotopy types.
